## Tier → Model Mapping (Pro+ only)

| Tier | Primary             | Fallback             | Why |
|------|---------------------|----------------------|-----|
| **S** (Strong)   | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | Architectural reasoning, safety-critical work, large context. Fallback keeps quality high while reducing premium-request spend if Opus quota is constrained. |
| **M** (Balanced) | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Best general-purpose code-gen + tool use on Pro+. `gpt-4.1` is unlimited on Pro+ and a reliable safety net. |
| **L** (Light)    | `claude-haiku-4.5`  | `gpt-4.1`            | Short prose, coordination, release notes. Haiku is fast and cheap; `gpt-4.1` fallback preserves quality if Haiku is unavailable. |

Rationale for the workhorse choice: `claude-sonnet-4.5` is consistently strong on
TypeScript / React code generation and multi-tool workflows — the exact shape of work
most of this team does — without burning the premium-request budget that Opus consumes.
Opus is reserved for the small set of agents whose mistakes are most expensive to undo
(schema, contract, privacy, cross-feature QA).

## Per-Agent Assignment

| Agent                          | Tier | Primary             | Fallback             | Rationale |
|--------------------------------|------|---------------------|----------------------|-----------|
| `redaction-engineer`           | S    | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | GDPR/SOC2 privacy surface (ADR-006). Wrong redaction = data leak. Highest determinism + safety bar in the team. |
| `provider-engineer`            | S    | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | Owns Zod schemas, schema versioning, the import orchestrator and dedup. Reads many providers + ADR-003 simultaneously — high reasoning + context. |
| `enrichment-engineer`          | S    | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | ADR-004 staged pipeline with "exactly once" semantics; touched by every sink. Mistakes ripple everywhere. |
| `sink-engineer`                | S    | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | ADR-005 `Sink` contract owner; changes break every downstream cloud / parquet / codeburn-export sink. |
| `qa-engineer`                  | S    | `claude-opus-4.5`   | `claude-sonnet-4.5`  | Cross-feature integration tests, ≥70% coverage gate (NF-04), strict-mode (NF-05), secret-scan, a11y. High context + safety. |
| `provider-engineer` _(repeat)_ |      |                     |                      | _(shown once above)_ |
| `analyzer-engineer`            | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Pure functions over enriched envelope. Self-contained, no cross-cutting blast radius. |
| `cli-engineer`                 | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Flag surface, JSON/table output, exit codes. Lots of small targeted code-gen; tool-use heavy. |
| `cloud-integration-engineer`   | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Cloud-side sinks (Azure → AWS → GCP); implements against ADR-005 rather than redefining it. |
| `datastore-engineer`           | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | On-disk JSONL format + idempotent writes. Borderline-S for format stability, but scope is narrow and well-bounded. |
| `observability-engineer`       | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Threshold rules + Teams/Slack notifications. Moderate complexity, low blast radius. |
| `plugin-marketplace-engineer`  | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Plugin hook system + manifest + marketplace workflow. Code-gen heavy across multiple subsystems. |
| `streaming-backend-engineer`   | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | Watcher, WebSocket/REST, backfill on reconnect. Borderline-S for concurrency reasoning; keeping at M because scope is contained to one feature. |
| `web-ui-engineer`              | M    | `claude-sonnet-4.5` | `gpt-4.1`            | React + TS dashboard, large code-gen volume, WCAG 2.1 AA. Sonnet excels at React/TS. |
| `release-manager`              | L    | `claude-haiku-4.5`  | `gpt-4.1`            | CHANGELOG, release notes, semver coordination, ADR amendments. Prose-heavy + workflow; Haiku is fast and sufficient. |

**Meta-agents intentionally untouched:**
`project-orchestrator` and `forge-team-builder` — per the skill, these are tooling, not
domain agents. They will continue to use your current default model. If you want them
assigned too, ask explicitly.

## Distribution Summary

- **Tier S:** 5 agents → `claude-opus-4.5`
- **Tier M:** 8 agents → `claude-sonnet-4.5`
- **Tier L:** 1 agent  → `claude-haiku-4.5`

Premium-request spend is concentrated on the 5 agents where a mistake costs the most
(privacy, schema, contract, derivation, QA). The 8 feature engineers run on the
unlimited-quality workhorse. The 1 prose/coordination agent runs on the fast tier.

## Launching with the Assigned Model (Copilot CLI)

For each agent, you can launch Copilot CLI with the matching model:

```bash
COPILOT_MODEL="claude-opus-4.5" copilot     # for a Tier S agent
COPILOT_MODEL="claude-sonnet-4.5" copilot   # for a Tier M agent
COPILOT_MODEL="claude-haiku-4.5" copilot    # for a Tier L agent
```

Per-agent launch wrappers (`.github/agents/_model-launch.sh` /
`.github/agents/_model-launch.ps1`) are **not** generated in Recommend mode. They will
be written if you confirm Apply.
